done.why: I put the egg in the trophy case by turn 36. After that I explored as far as I could. The dam, the canyon view, the flooded passages and the hole under the altar were all closed off, and the thief killed me in his Treasure Room. When I came back, the egg was still in the case and every edge I tried led to a sign or to water, so I left.

about: The white house and the Great Underground Empire, cut down to a smaller area. You collect treasures and bring them home to a trophy case that seems to be waiting for them. Underground there's a troll, a twisty maze, a cyclops you can scare off with the right name, and a thief who guards his hoard and will kill you over it. The edges of the map are closed in polite ways: dam inspection notices, scenery company signs, and passages that sink into black water.

ending.what: The egg went into the trophy case at turn 36 and was listed as part of my collection, which was my goal. The game didn't announce an ending. It gave me 20 points and kept going. Later the thief killed me. The world brought me back and the egg was still in the case.

moments.note: The trophy case has 'the patient air of something that expects to be filled.' That was a nice way to show me what to do.
The egg was right in the nest. The extra line about a songbird with 'better taste in treasure than in architecture' made me smile.
Putting the egg in the case just said 'Done.' I'd met my goal and nothing marked it until I typed score.
The trap door crashed shut and someone barred it behind me.
I couldn't take the platinum bar because my load was too heavy, 'the sword not least of it.' I never went back for it.
The dam was closed with a sign: 'CLOSED FOR INSPECTION -- The Management.' I found it funny, but it was a wall.
The northwest passage, and later the chasm path, both ran into still black water. I couldn't tell if this was a puzzle or just the edge of the map.
The hole under the altar wouldn't let me in. It had lovely prose about sighing voices, but it was closed.
Praying at the altar took me back to the forest, which got me out of the temple.
The chimney's carry limit was explained clearly: 'room for you, your lamp and one thing more.'
Saying 'odysseus' scared the cyclops off through a wall.
The thief rushed in to defend his hideaway and knocked my sword out of my hand straight away.
The thief killed me in two exchanges. I hadn't been warned he was that dangerous.
The death text was kind and specific: plain things scattered around the house, valuables rolled into dark corners, and 'somebody tidy has put the lamp back.'
After I died the egg, torch, sceptre and painting were all still safe in the case.
Another closed edge: 'CANYON VIEW CLOSED FOR REPAIRS.'

wished: I wanted to get through the dam, the black water, or the hole under the altar. A completionist hits too many closed doors here.
I wanted to carry the platinum bar out without leaving half my kit behind.
I wanted some acknowledgement when the egg went into the case, since that was the whole point.
I wanted to be able to open the egg. I had 'neither the tools nor the expertise.'
I wanted a fair chance against the thief, or a hint that walking into his room with a sword was a bad idea.
I wanted to find out where the bag of coins rolled after I died.

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: It quietly told me what the game wants from me.

lines.line: wedged into the fork of a branch by a songbird with better taste in treasure than in architecture.
You decide that whatever is down there has waited this long and can wait a little longer.
lines.why: A closed door written as a choice I made rather than a wall, though it's still a wall.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: It told me the exact rule. That's fair puzzling.

lines.line: anything of value has rolled into some dark corner in or under it, and somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: A warm, wry way to handle death, and it told me where to look for my things.

fun.why: Getting the egg was quick and satisfying. The temple, the prayer exit, the gallery, the maze and the cyclops were all fun to find. Dying to the thief stung, and the many closed-off edges took some of the fun away.

engagement.why: I wanted to see every room and I kept pushing deeper. My interest dropped each time a passage ended at a sign or at black water.

difficulty.why: The egg itself was easy: open the window, climb the tree, put it in the case. The weight limit and the chimney limit added a bit of friction. The thief fight was the one really hard part.

interestingness.why: It's a familiar world with new touches: a talkative trophy case, explained carry limits, a forgiving death that tidies up after you, and the thief defending his hoard. The closed edges felt deliberate and had personality.

prose.why: The new lines are vivid and dry and fit the old tone well. Many responses are bare ('Done.', 'Taken.'), and the important moment of putting the egg in the case had none of that warmth.
